query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: rating_consistency
per_column.rationale: A descriptive summary of dispersion across the existing sub-ratings (High/Moderate/Consistent variance). It is neither a distinct candidate cause of non-recommendation nor a common cause of any treatment and the outcome; it is a derived meta-feature of the same ratings that largely determine recommendation. Not a confounder.

per_column.name: value_perception
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause of the outcome: poor/premium-price-complaint value plausibly drives a non-recommendation. Derived from Value For Money plus review text. This is one of the treatments whose effect is being attributed, not a confounder (it is not shown to cause any other treatment).

per_column.name: service_gap
per_column.rationale: Identifies which service dimension was weak (food/seat/IFE/staff/multiple). This is a direct candidate cause of non-recommendation surfaced from the sub-ratings. It functions as a treatment, not a confounder or mediator of another treatment.

per_column.name: experience_score
per_column.rationale: A numeric composite/average of the sub-ratings, i.e. an aggregate proxy for overall satisfaction sitting on the causal path between the specific experience factors and the recommendation decision. Adjusting for it would block the very effects being attributed; it is a mediator/proxy, not a confounder.

per_column.name: issue_type
per_column.rationale: Categorises the primary complaint (operational/ground/compensation/product-quality) extracted from review text. A candidate cause of non-recommendation, hence a treatment. It is not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome, so not a confounder.

judge.rationale: The operator supplied a rich set of CANDIDATE CAUSES (value_perception, service_gap, issue_type) plus an aggregate mediator (experience_score) and a descriptive dispersion feature (rating_consistency). So the 'treatment' half of a causal setup is present and even over-supplied. However, the decisive requirement for causal ATTRIBUTION is missing: there are NO confounders — no added variable is a common cause of BOTH a treatment and the non-recommendation outcome. Genuine confounders for this question (e.g., type of traveller, route/market, month/season flown, verified status, prior loyalty/expectation level, cabin/aircraft variant) were NOT surfaced as new columns; several such candidates already sit in the original table and none were adjusted-for or elevated. Because the columns are almost entirely treatments and mediators/proxies of the outcome, they cannot support an unbiased effect estimate — attributing non-recommendation to value_perception or service_gap without confounder control would be biased. The capability under test (surfacing confounders from the data/text rather than copying them from the query) is therefore NOT demonstrated, and confounder_quality is 0.
